title: BattlEye in 2019: four components, one moving detection surface
summary: A reading of vmcall's 2019 BattlEye investigation, separating the in-game detection module from the service, driver and backend. The observed shellcode and reports are a dated sample, not a current inventory of BattlEye.
author: Observatory editorial
takeaways: Distinguish the service, kernel driver, game-resident client and server before assigning a detection to a component.
The published 2019 shellcode snapshot shows local memory inspection and reports; it does not reveal present-day enforcement logic.
An executable-memory anomaly is a signal requiring context, not proof that a player cheated.
